newsitem.title: INDIA: Thailand will strongly defend baht - Chatichai.
newsitem.headline: Thailand will strongly defend baht - Chatichai.

text.p: Former Thai prime minister Chatichai Choonhavan, who leads the second largest party in the ruling coalition, said on Wednesday that the government will strongly defend the value of the baht.
"Strongly we will defend the value of our baht," Chatichai, who leads the Chart Pattana Party (CPP), told the Confederation of Indian Industry.
Chatichai was visiting India as a special emissary of Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh and was accompanied by a 10-member delegation.
Asked if the government would be well advised to expand the basket of currencies linked to the baht, Chatichai said: "Not at this time."
He said the Bank of Thailand estimates that gross domestic product (GDP) will grow by 5.9 percent in 1997, down from 6.4 percent last year.
"Our economic fundamentals remain sound, and foreign investors are confident in the Thai economy's resilience," he said.
